brief: Goldman's systematic dispersion suite had a strong 2026, driven by the AI-narrative-fueled single-stock/index implied-vol dislocation and sector rotation: implied correlation sat near historical lows while realized correlation fell even further, so dispersion delivered strong risk-adjusted returns. Single-stock vol buyers were paid simultaneously as earnings jumps (AMZN +15.32% Jul 31, MSFT +15.51% Jul 30, NVDA +7.87% Feb 6) exceeded implied moves, a goldilocks combination. Decomposing realized correlation, GS finds inter-sector correlation compressed to ~0% by late summer, the year's most extreme reading, while intra-sector correlation stayed range-bound, a stock-picker's market within sectors; GS sees continued room for dispersion as between-sector compression remains the driver. The flagship GSVIDUG6 strategy ran up 20%+ Apr-Jul before giving back gains in the early-August vol meltdown; post-reset, GS argues implied spread is now lower, catalysts (earnings dispersion, AI rotation, elevated LETF shares outstanding) persist, and a repeat of the January-July run is unlikely but that should not discourage putting dispersion on now. The note also details downside, NDX, thematic and dynamic dispersion variants and a reworked shock-analysis framework correcting the standard practice's overstatement of stress losses.
